newsitem.title: UK: Competition pressures Lloyd's rates lower - survey.
newsitem.headline: Competition pressures Lloyd's rates lower - survey.

text.p: Competition and the availability of cheap reinsurance are ensuring that the downward cycle for prices is continuing for most classes of business within Lloyds of London, members' agent LRG Cater Allen said.
Based on a survey of 23 underwriters in the insurance market, only motor rates are showing any signs of firming, the agency said in its January newsletter.
Even here, "underwriters expect increases to be small and steady rather than the huge increases that took place in 1993."
Rates are more or less stable in a few areas, including marine cargo and aviation liability and excess of loss business.
In most other areas of marine, non-marine and aviation the underwriters surveyed said rates were falling, with some of the biggest declines -- up to 50 percent -- on marine hull accounts.
Much of the rate cutting was made possible by "extensive and cheap" reinsurance, the members' agent said.

Another feature of the survey was the observation by non-marine and aviation underwriters that their marine counterparts were moving into other classes of business where they were behind much of the aggressive price cutting.
Marine underwriters said the most severe competition in their market was from large Lloyd's syndicates and the international company market seeking to acquire high volume business.
LRG Cater Allen said, "at times like these, underwriters need to stick to the areas of business in which they are skilled leaders."
